metaDescription: Four 30 inch battery lawn mowers compared: walk-behind and compact riding designs, torque, runtime, slope handling and what suits half-acre lawns.
expertTake: The EGO Power+ 30 inch Super Composite mower is the best overall because its 13.2 ft-lbs of torque, 75 minutes of claimed runtime and Touch Drive suit large lawns without engine upkeep. The Toro eTimeMaster is the value pick if you already own 60V batteries. If your lawn is under a third of an acre, a 30 inch deck is overkill, and a 21 inch mower will store easier and cost far less.
introParagraphs: A wide-deck mower is a big step up from the standard walk-behind size. It cuts a much wider path per pass and shortens mowing time on larger lawns, but it also demands more motor torque, more battery and a gate wide enough to get it into the yard.

This guide explains how deck width changes power demands, why runtime claims vary so much, and how walk-behind and compact riding formats differ on slopes. Use the picks above for a quick shortlist, then read the reviews below for the tradeoffs on each.

products.name: EGO Power+ 30 Inch Super Composite Self-Propelled Mower Kit

specList.label: Torque
specList.value: Up to 13.2 ft-lbs with Peak Power

products.description:
The EGO 30 inch is the most complete wide-deck walk-behind here. Peak Power combines two 56V batteries to deliver up to 13.2 ft-lbs of cutting torque, which EGO compares to gas engines above 200cc. That torque is what keeps a 30 inch blade at speed in thick, tall grass, where a wide deck is most likely to bog.

The Super Composite deck is optimized for torque and blade speed and is lighter than steel, which helps maneuvering. Two 6.0Ah batteries are claimed to cut up to 75 minutes, enough for most half-acre lawns. Touch Drive puts self-propel control under your palm, so you adjust speed with pressure rather than a lever.

Compared with the Toro, which is sold without batteries, the EGO is a complete kit. Batteries are shared across the EGO family. Wash the deck underside, keep the blades sharp and store the packs indoors.
products.bestFor: Half-acre lawns where you want a wide deck, strong torque and no engine upkeep.
pros: 13.2 ft-lbs of torque handles thick, tall grass
Two 6.0Ah batteries claim up to 75 minutes
Touch Drive adjusts pace with palm pressure
Lightweight composite deck is easier to maneuver
cons: 30 in width needs a wide gate for access
Thick grass cuts runtime well below the claim

products.name: Toro 60V MAX 30 Inch eTimeMaster Personal Pace Mower (Tool Only)
products.description:
The eTimeMaster is a bare-tool mower for Toro 60V MAX batteries, with a 30 inch deck and a dual-blade system. Dual Force uses two blades that mulch clippings into finer pieces, which gives a cleaner cut and quicker breakdown on the lawn.

Personal Pace drive adjusts the self-propel speed to how fast you walk, so you control the mower by pace rather than a speed dial. Toro claims you can save up to 40 percent of mowing time versus a standard deck, a figure that follows from the width.

Because batteries are not included, the total cost depends on what you own. Compared with the EGO kit, you must buy at least one 60V pack and a charger. Toro has a strong dealer network, which helps parts and service. Keep the deck clean and store batteries indoors.
products.bestFor: Toro 60V owners who already have batteries and want a wide-deck walk-behind.
pros: Personal Pace drive follows your walking speed
Dual blade system mulches clippings finely
Push-button start and dual LED headlights
cons: Torque and runtime are not specified
Total cost jumps if you need batteries

products.name: Greenworks Commercial 30 Inch Optimus Self-Propelled Mower Kit
products.description:
Greenworks builds this around independent dual hub motors, which let each rear wheel drive separately and keep the mower tracking straight across slopes up to 25 degrees. That is a real engineering advantage over single-motor drive when you are mowing sideways on a hill.

A 30 inch steel deck houses counter-rotating dual motors with a claimed 16,000 feet per minute blade tip speed, which helps cut quality and aerodynamics for mulching and bagging. Greenworks rates the motors as more powerful than a 230cc gas engine. Three 8Ah batteries and a dual-port charger give a large energy reserve.

A tool-only version of the same machine is also listed, so you can save if you own the batteries. Compared with the EGO, it focuses on commercial-style durability and slope control. Wash the deck after each use.
products.bestFor: Hilly lawns where straight tracking on a slope matters most.
pros: Dual hub motors keep tracking straight on slopes
Counter-rotating motors reach 16,000 FPM blade tip speed
Three 8Ah batteries provide a large energy reserve
Steel deck is built for commercial-style use
cons: Heavier and more complex than single-motor mowers
Premium cost compared with consumer walk-behinds

products.name: Greenworks 60V 30 Inch Riding Lawn Mower
products.description:
This is a compact riding mower, not a walk-behind, and it changes the economics of a large lawn. A 30 inch 4-in-1 stamped steel deck with an integrated wash port cuts, mulches, bags or side-discharges, and a single lever sets seven heights from 1.5 to 4.5 inches.

Four 8.0Ah 60V batteries give a claimed 1.25 acres per charge, and Greenworks rates the single brushless cutting motor as a 16 HP gas equivalent. A 6 MPH top speed and a 200 pound towing rating make it useful for hauling small loads.

Compared with the walk-behind picks, it saves your legs, but needs storage space and a larger investment. Keep the deck clean and store the batteries indoors in winter.
products.bestFor: Large lawns where riding saves effort and you want battery power.
pros: Riding format saves effort on a large lawn
Four 8.0Ah batteries claim up to 1.25 acres
Integrated deck wash port eases cleanup
Single-lever height adjustment across seven positions
cons: Needs garage space compared with walk-behinds
Coverage claim depends on grass condition
Higher cost than the walk-behind options

buyingCriteria.explanation: A 30 inch walk-behind covers more ground than a 21 inch mower per pass but you still walk behind it, which is tiring on a half-acre or more. A compact riding mower saves your legs and tows small loads, but needs storage and costs more. If your lawn is under three quarters of an acre, a self-propelled walk-behind is usually enough. The EGO, Toro and Greenworks Optimus are walk-behinds, and the Greenworks riding model rides.

A 30 inch blade is long, so it needs more torque to hold speed in thick grass. Underpowered wide decks bog and leave streaks. Look for high torque or a gas-equivalent rating. The EGO claims up to 13.2 ft-lbs with Peak Power, and Greenworks rates the Optimus as stronger than a 230cc gas engine and the riding mower as a 16 HP equivalent.

Mowing demand scales with deck width, so a wide-deck battery mower needs more stored energy. Compare total amp-hours and the number of packs, not voltage alone. The EGO includes two 6.0Ah packs for a claimed 75 minutes, the Optimus three 8Ah packs and the riding mower four 8.0Ah packs.

On a slope, weight shifts and wheels lose traction. Independent hub motors, rear-wheel drive and a low center of gravity keep a mower tracking. The Greenworks Optimus rates 25 degrees with dual hub motors. Always mow across slopes with a walk-behind and up and down with a rider.

Steel decks are strong and inexpensive but rust, composite decks resist rust and dents and are lighter, and aluminum is stiff and rust-proof. Wide decks flex more, so material matters. The EGO uses Super Composite, and the Optimus and riding Greenworks use steel.
A 30 inch deck needs a gate and shed door at least that wide plus clearance for handles. Measure before you buy. Riding mowers need garage space. Many buyers realize this after delivery.

cards.label: Walk-behind
cards.text: Lower cost, easy storage and precise control. The EGO, Toro and Greenworks Optimus fall here, but long sessions tire your legs.

cards.label: Riding
cards.text: Saves effort and tows small loads, but needs space and costs more. The Greenworks 60V riding mower falls here.

howToChoose.note: Choose walk-behind up to about three quarters of an acre, and riding beyond.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Independent wheel drive or a rider with a low center of gravity, and a rated slope angle.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Greenworks Optimus is rated for 25 degrees with dual hub motors, and the EGO's Touch Drive helps traction on moderate slopes.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: Your lawn is near an acre or hilly. The Greenworks Optimus or riding mower save time and effort.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: Your lawn is under half an acre. The Toro with batteries you own or a smaller mower is enough.

maintenance.why: A dull blade tears grass and strains the motor. Wide decks magnify the effect.
Packed clippings cause clogging and rust. Disconnect the battery first.
Lithium packs age fastest empty or hot. Keep them indoors.
Low pressure and worn tires reduce traction. Replace as needed.
Vibration loosens fasteners. A loose blade is a safety hazard.

faq.q: Is a 30 inch mower too big for a suburban lawn?
faq.a: For lawns under a third of an acre, yes, since storage and access become issues. For half an acre or more, it saves real time.
Tool-only units cost less if you own the platform. Full kits and riding models cost more. Count batteries in the total.

faq.q: How long does a battery last?
faq.a: Claims range from about 75 minutes on two 6.0Ah packs to a claimed 1.25 acres on four 8.0Ah packs. Thick grass shortens runtime.

faq.q: Do I need a riding mower?
faq.a: Above about three quarters of an acre, a riding mower saves effort. Below that, a self-propelled walk-behind is enough.
They are marketing comparisons. Judge by torque, battery capacity and owner feedback.
Wear sturdy shoes and eye protection, clear stones and toys, and remove the battery before cleaning the deck.
